Role: lead-po. Process: feature-authoring, step draft. Working directory: /home/vscode/rebaseline. You have Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob — no shell; the lead-pm computes the scenario hashes after you (write `@hash:pending` on each scenario).

Inputs
- initiative: initiatives/init-typedef-rendering.md (planned, v9). Its Framing and For whom are the source of the Feature line and narrative; its Appetite names the proof: the product decision record, made by the PO and screened by its check from the same standard.
- repository: features/ (three features exist; features/feat-request-routing.md is the most recent form — match its structure: Feature line and narrative, the Gherkin block with tags, Contributors, Interaction types, Edges, Document History).

What good looks like (the checker applies basis/fitness/feature.fitness.md — read it; the six scenarios: each scenario one observable behavior, Given/When/Then with the When one action or event and the Then observable; ownership and criteria present; identity tags present — `@feature:feat-typedef-rendering @hash:<12 hex>`; every listed edge covered by a named scenario or excluded with a reason; interaction types stated; the feature says who it is for and why). Also basis/artifacts/feature.md §Required sections.

Behavior to cover, from the initiative (say what, never how; no tool names, file names, or technology in scenario text — "renders" and "compiler" are mechanism, so say the effect: the maker's text and the checker's text exist for a type and match its one standard):
1. For an artifact type, one standard exists and both the maker's text and the checker's text derive from it (the reader can tell each is produced from the standard and is current with it).
2. The checker's tests keep their form (Given/When/Then) and an author can run them on their own draft before the check.
3. When the standard changes, both the maker's and the checker's text change with it, and a text that no longer matches its standard is detectable.
4. The proof: the product decision record for this initiative's bet is made by the PO from the maker's text and screened by its check from the checker's text — the same standard, both used once.
5. A type whose standard has no writer's guidance or no tests today still has both texts once its standard says what it says (the batch case), or states that none is due.
6. Nothing a check does changes; only what it reads.
Edges: a hand edit to a produced text; a standard changed without its texts following; a type with no guideline or fitness set today; an author skipping the self-run; the batch of the other 21 types (out of scope of this feature — the second bet; state it).
Contributors: shopsystem-product for every scenario (the Decomposition names no Bounded Context); leave the designer's and architect's criteria for their own steps. Interaction types: none, per the initiative's For whom, with its reason.

Write features/feat-typedef-rendering.md (status draft, version 1, owner lead-po, initiative ../initiatives/init-typedef-rendering.md, one history row). Then edit only the "## Features" section of the initiative: replace "None yet." with "[feat-typedef-rendering](../features/feat-typedef-rendering.md) — draft." Do not use these words: ratify, ratified, ratification, disposition, surface, seat. Before returning, read your draft against the six scenarios as the checker would and fix what you find; say what you fixed. Return the path, the scenario count with one line each, and the fixes.

13	# Feature: Request routing and the small-change lane
14	
15	## Feature
16	
17	Feature: Request routing and the small-change lane
18	  The product authority, and anyone bringing the lead shop an ask,
19	  can bring an ask and see it recorded on arrival with a decided
20	  route — into a discovery conversation, to a simple change (the
21	  small-change lane), or declined with the authority — and can take a
22	  simple change to a
23	  verified result without the stages that protect a bet,
24	  so that getting simple things done no longer requires the full
25	  product flow.
26	
27	## Contributors
28	
29	Owning shop, per scenario — from the initiative's Decomposition
30	section, which names no Bounded Context: every amended definition and
31	the example change sit in the lead shop's tree, and no contract exists
32	on this branch to rely on.
33	
34	- *an ask brought to the lead shop is recorded as a request on arrival* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
35	- *an ask arising in open conversation is recorded as a request* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
36	- *open conversation that makes no ask leaves no request* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
37	- *an ask arising inside another process is recorded as a request* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
38	- *a request not yet routed is visible as awaiting its route* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
39	- *a recorded request has a decided route* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
40	- *an objection to the route is answered before the route is acted on* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
41	- *a route said but not answered is recorded as said and not acted on* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
42	- *a request routed into discovery is the discovery conversation's input* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
43	- *the initiative made from a request references the request* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
44	- *a simple change is defined up front before it is made* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
45	- *a simple change is checked by a role other than its maker* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
46	- *a simple change reaches a verified result with no bet and no check of record* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
47	- *a request whose change turns out not simple is routed to discovery* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
48	- *a declined ask is settled with the authority and its record survives* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
49	- *the example change reaches a verified result through the lane* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
50	
51	Vocabulary: *ask* is the framing's word for one expression of intent
52	brought to the lead shop by an originator (glossary: `intent`,
53	`originator`); it is not the glossary's `ask` — the question one
54	activity puts to another role. *Request* is the artifact type of the
55	same name, the record an ask becomes on arrival. *The small-change
56	lane* is the initiative's name for the route a simple change takes;
57	*check of record* is the glossary's term for what the initiative's
58	Appetite calls the screen of record. A change is *simple* when it
59	spends no appetite worth a bet: it stays within the lead shop's own
60	definitions or one instance of them, touches no Bounded Context, and
61	its effect is demonstrable in the running system in one session; the
62	lead-pm role judges this at routing, and the lead-po role may find
63	otherwise once the change is defined, which changes the request's
64	route to a discovery conversation with the reason. In the lane, the
65	lead-po role defines a simple change — its definition is a
66	requirement; the role that makes the change is its *maker*; the check
67	sits with a role other than the maker. *The intake process* is the process in which an ask is
68	recorded as a request and routed — the router's process, distinct
69	from the lane and from the discovery conversation.
70	
71	Usability acceptance criteria — due: the initiative's For whom section
72	names the conversational type. Judged against the experience principle
73	set and the core-task list; they stand on the "make a request"
74	hypothesis stated under Interaction types, and each says what must
75	hold for the originator — the product authority or anyone bringing an
76	ask — at the conversational door, not how the door is built. The door
77	is an assistant interaction (glossary): the product acts on a stated
78	intent, so `control-stays-with-the-person` binds it. The router is the
79	lead-pm role, as the scenarios name it. (designer, 2026-09-04)
80	
81	- U1 — the task's three options hold at the door (`core-task-parity`):
82	  the originator states the ask in their own words and the request
83	  records those words, not a paraphrase; the originator is given the
84	  request's id in the same turn the record is confirmed, alongside the
85	  words and never in place of them; the originator can read the route
86	  and its reason from the door. Rides on *an ask brought to the lead
87	  shop is recorded as a request on arrival*, *an ask arising in open
88	  conversation is recorded as a request*, *a recorded request has a
89	  decided route*.
90	- U2 — the door says what it can do (`control-stays-with-the-person`,
91	  first bullet): the originator can learn from the door, without
92	  leaving it, that an ask is recorded on arrival and the three routes
93	  it can take — a discovery conversation, the small-change lane,
94	  declined — with what each means. Rides on *an ask brought to the
95	  lead shop is recorded as a request on arrival*, *a recorded request
96	  has a decided route*.
97	- U3 — the router's reading is said before it is recorded
98	  (`control-stays-with-the-person`, third and fourth bullets): when
99	  open conversation's words are read as an ask, the door says so
100	  before a request is recorded; the originator's "no" leaves no
101	  request; when the router cannot tell, it asks rather than records;
102	  silence is not a yes. Rides on *an ask arising in open conversation
103	  is recorded as a request*, *open conversation that makes no ask
104	  leaves no request*.
105	- U4 — the route is said before it is acted on
106	  (`control-stays-with-the-person`, second and third bullets): the
107	  originator hears the route and its reason before a discovery
108	  conversation opens on the request, the lane takes it up, or a
109	  decline is settled; an objection the originator makes then is heard
110	  before action, the route recorded is the one standing after it, and
111	  its reason answers the objection — the decision stays the lead-pm
112	  role's. A request stays visibly awaiting its route until the route
113	  is said; no route is taken because the originator did not answer. A
114	  route changed later is read with its reason the same way the first
115	  was. Rides on *a recorded request has a decided route*, *a request
116	  not yet routed is visible as awaiting its route*, *a request whose
117	  change turns out not simple is routed to discovery*.
118	- U5 — an ask arising mid-run neither derails the run nor vanishes:
119	  the person present hears, in one turn, that the ask was recorded
120	  with its id and that the run continues without acting on it. Rides
121	  on *an ask arising inside another process is recorded as a request*.
122	- U6 — the decline guides recovery (`errors-guide-recovery`): the
123	  decline is said in the originator's natural language — that the ask
124	  was declined, that the authority ruled, and the reason — with what
125	  the originator can do next; a reason is never a code, a work-item id, or
126	  a route name alone. Rides on *a declined ask is settled with the
127	  authority and its record survives*.
128	- U7 — one vocabulary (`consistent-not-uniform`): the record is called
129	  a request and the routes are named as this feature names them — the
130	  same words at the door, on the request, in the list of requests awaiting a route, and in
131	  the discovery conversation opened on the request; the originator is
132	  never asked to restate an ask the request already holds. Rides on
133	  *a request not yet routed is visible as awaiting its route*, *a
134	  recorded request has a decided route*, *a request routed into
135	  discovery is the discovery conversation's input*.
136	
137	Evidence (`evidence-not-opinion`): these criteria and the hypothesis
138	they stand on rest on no observed use; the door's usability is a
139	hypothesis at delivery until a user test or measured task completion
140	is recorded. A usability test invalidates the scenarios U1, U4, and
141	U6 ride on when an originator, after the router's turn, cannot say
142	whether a request was recorded, which route was taken or how to
143	object to it, or what to do after a decline. (designer, 2026-09-04)
144	
145	Accessibility criteria — the conversational door is a non-web
146	assistant interaction: `accessible-by-standard`'s second bullet
147	applies the WCAG 2.2 success criteria as WCAG2ICT describes for
148	non-web software, with an applicability record; its third bullet sets
149	conformance before delivery. (designer, 2026-09-04)
150	
151	- A1 — meaning in words (SC 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics and 1.4.1
152	  Use of Color, as applied): the record's confirmation, the id, the
153	  route, and the reason are conveyed in text; nothing the originator
154	  needs is carried by colour, symbol, position, or sound alone. Rides
155	  on *an ask brought to the lead shop is recorded as a request on
156	  arrival*, *an ask arising in open conversation is recorded as a
157	  request*, *a recorded request has a decided route*, *a declined ask
158	  is settled with the authority and its record survives*.
159	- A2 — no time limit on the originator's turn (SC 2.2.1 Timing
160	  Adjustable, as applied): the router's question — whether words are
161	  an ask, whether the route stands — waits for the originator; no
162	  request is recorded and no route acted on because a time ran out.
163	  Rides on *open conversation that makes no ask leaves no request*,
164	  *a request not yet routed is visible as awaiting its route*, *a
165	  recorded request has a decided route*.
166	- A3 — consistent identification (SC 3.2.4, as applied): the request,
167	  its id, and each route are named the same way every time the door
168	  says them and wherever the request is read. Rides on *a request not
169	  yet routed is visible as awaiting its route*, *a recorded request
170	  has a decided route*, *a request routed into discovery is the
171	  discovery conversation's input*, *a request whose change turns out
172	  not simple is routed to discovery*.
173	- A4 — errors identified with a way forward (SC 3.3.1 Error
174	  Identification and 3.3.3 Error Suggestion, as applied): a misread
175	  ask, a changed route, and a decline are described in text with what
176	  the originator can do. Rides on *open conversation that makes no ask
177	  leaves no request*, *a request whose change turns out not simple is
178	  routed to discovery*, *a declined ask is settled with the authority
179	  and its record survives*.
180	- A5 — no redundant entry (SC 3.3.7, as applied): an originator whose
181	  ask is recorded is not asked to state it again for it to be routed
182	  or for discovery to open on it — the request is read. Rides on *a
183	  recorded request has a decided route*, *a request routed into
184	  discovery is the discovery conversation's input*.
185	- A6 — the applicability record: before the door is delivered, the
186	  record of which WCAG 2.2 success criteria do not apply to the
187	  conversational type and why stands in the experience guidance
188	  corpus, and an accessibility result at the target is attached with
189	  the delivery; a delivery gate the check the experience guidance
190	  corpus defines for an interaction judges, not a scenario's behavior.

192	Non-functional constraints — due. The initiative's Decomposition
193	names no Bounded Context, so no cross-context constraint applies;
194	what it does name is a bound — every amended definition and the

196	this branch to rely on — and the architecture decision record the
197	initiative rests on,
198	[adr-2026-09-04-request-front-end](../decisions/adr-2026-09-04-request-front-end.md)
199	(checked, v4), sets the guardrails an implementation of these

202	each rides on the scenarios it bounds. (architect, 2026-09-04)

204	- C1 — the request is the existing root type, amended (the ADR's
205	  declined third option; the initiative's no-go "we are not working
206	  through any new types"): the record an ask becomes is an instance
207	  of the `request` artifact type as its typedef stands amended to

209	  the route with its reason, and where the route led — and no new
210	  artifact type is introduced for the received ask, for the simple
211	  change's definition, or for its verified result. The amendment is
212	  made to the typedef, by its owner, with its Document History row,
213	  before any instance relies on what it admits. Rides on *an ask
214	  brought to the lead shop is recorded as a request on arrival*, *an
215	  ask arising in open conversation is recorded as a request*, *an ask
216	  arising inside another process is recorded as a request*, *a
217	  recorded request has a decided route*, *a declined ask is settled
218	  with the authority and its record survives*, *a simple change is
219	  defined up front before it is made*, *a simple change reaches a

221	- C2 — the request is the durable record, in the repository (the
222	  ADR's decision): a request stands as a governed artifact in this
223	  branch's tree from the moment it is recorded, declined asks
224	  included. A work-register item, a session record, or a transcript
225	  is not the record of an ask; an ask that exists only in one of
226	  these is not recorded, and "recorded" in every scenario's Then
227	  means this. Rides on *an ask brought to the lead shop is recorded
228	  as a request on arrival*, *an ask arising in open conversation is
229	  recorded as a request*, *an ask arising inside another process is
230	  recorded as a request*, *a request not yet routed is visible as

239	  *a request not yet routed is visible as awaiting its route*, *a

242	  request*, *a simple change is defined up front before it is made*,

251	  routed into discovery is the discovery conversation's input*, *a

253	  change reaches a verified result with no bet and no check of

258	  consequences): the request is the same record whichever lead-shop
259	  role meets the ask and whoever fills that role — the authority in

334	## Interaction types

# Feature: Request routing and the small-change lane

## Feature

Feature: Request routing and the small-change lane
  The product authority, and anyone bringing the lead shop an ask,
  can bring an ask and see it recorded on arrival with a decided
  route — into a discovery conversation, to a simple change (the
  small-change lane), or declined with the authority — and can take a
  simple change to a
  verified result without the stages that protect a bet,
  so that getting simple things done no longer requires the full
  product flow.

## Contributors

Owning shop, per scenario — from the initiative's Decomposition
section, which names no Bounded Context: every amended definition and
the example change sit in the lead shop's tree, and no contract exists
on this branch to rely on.

Vocabulary: *ask* is the framing's word for one expression of intent
brought to the lead shop by an originator (glossary: `intent`,
`originator`); it is not the glossary's `ask` — the question one
activity puts to another role. *Request* is the artifact type of the
same name, the record an ask becomes on arrival. *The small-change
lane* is the initiative's name for the route a simple change takes;
*check of record* is the glossary's term for what the initiative's
Appetite calls the screen of record. A change is *simple* when it
spends no appetite worth a bet: it stays within the lead shop's own
definitions or one instance of them, touches no Bounded Context, and
its effect is demonstrable in the running system in one session; the
lead-pm role judges this at routing, and the lead-po role may find
otherwise once the change is defined, which changes the request's
route to a discovery conversation with the reason. In the lane, the
lead-po role defines a simple change — its definition is a
requirement; the role that makes the change is its *maker*; the check
sits with a role other than the maker. *The intake process* is the process in which an ask is
recorded as a request and routed — the router's process, distinct
from the lane and from the discovery conversation.

Usability acceptance criteria — due: the initiative's For whom section
names the conversational type. Judged against the experience principle
set and the core-task list; they stand on the "make a request"
hypothesis stated under Interaction types, and each says what must
hold for the originator — the product authority or anyone bringing an
ask — at the conversational door, not how the door is built. The door
is an assistant interaction (glossary): the product acts on a stated
intent, so `control-stays-with-the-person` binds it. The router is the
lead-pm role, as the scenarios name it. (designer, 2026-09-04)

- U1 — the task's three options hold at the door (`core-task-parity`):
  the originator states the ask in their own words and the request
  records those words, not a paraphrase; the originator is given the
  request's id in the same turn the record is confirmed, alongside the
  words and never in place of them; the originator can read the route
  and its reason from the door. Rides on *an ask brought to the lead
  shop is recorded as a request on arrival*, *an ask arising in open
  conversation is recorded as a request*, *a recorded request has a
  decided route*.
- U2 — the door says what it can do (`control-stays-with-the-person`,
  first bullet): the originator can learn from the door, without
  leaving it, that an ask is recorded on arrival and the three routes
  it can take — a discovery conversation, the small-change lane,
  declined — with what each means. Rides on *an ask brought to the
  lead shop is recorded as a request on arrival*, *a recorded request
  has a decided route*.
- U3 — the router's reading is said before it is recorded
  (`control-stays-with-the-person`, third and fourth bullets): when
  open conversation's words are read as an ask, the door says so
  before a request is recorded; the originator's "no" leaves no
  request; when the router cannot tell, it asks rather than records;
  silence is not a yes. Rides on *an ask arising in open conversation
  is recorded as a request*, *open conversation that makes no ask
  leaves no request*.
- U4 — the route is said before it is acted on
  (`control-stays-with-the-person`, second and third bullets): the
  originator hears the route and its reason before a discovery
  conversation opens on the request, the lane takes it up, or a
  decline is settled; an objection the originator makes then is heard
  before action, the route recorded is the one standing after it, and
  its reason answers the objection — the decision stays the lead-pm
  role's. A request stays visibly awaiting its route until the route
  is said; no route is taken because the originator did not answer. A
  route changed later is read with its reason the same way the first
  was. Rides on *a recorded request has a decided route*, *a request
  not yet routed is visible as awaiting its route*, *a request whose
  change turns out not simple is routed to discovery*.
- U5 — an ask arising mid-run neither derails the run nor vanishes:
  the person present hears, in one turn, that the ask was recorded
  with its id and that the run continues without acting on it. Rides
  on *an ask arising inside another process is recorded as a request*.
- U6 — the decline guides recovery (`errors-guide-recovery`): the
  decline is said in the originator's natural language — that the ask
  was declined, that the authority ruled, and the reason — with what
  the originator can do next; a reason is never a code, a work-item id, or
  a route name alone. Rides on *a declined ask is settled with the
  authority and its record survives*.
- U7 — one vocabulary (`consistent-not-uniform`): the record is called
  a request and the routes are named as this feature names them — the
  same words at the door, on the request, in the list of requests awaiting a route, and in
  the discovery conversation opened on the request; the originator is
  never asked to restate an ask the request already holds. Rides on
  *a request not yet routed is visible as awaiting its route*, *a
  recorded request has a decided route*, *a request routed into
  discovery is the discovery conversation's input*.

Evidence (`evidence-not-opinion`): these criteria and the hypothesis
they stand on rest on no observed use; the door's usability is a
hypothesis at delivery until a user test or measured task completion
is recorded. A usability test invalidates the scenarios U1, U4, and
U6 ride on when an originator, after the router's turn, cannot say
whether a request was recorded, which route was taken or how to
object to it, or what to do after a decline. (designer, 2026-09-04)

Accessibility criteria — the conversational door is a non-web
assistant interaction: `accessible-by-standard`'s second bullet

## Interaction types

Conversational — the initiative's For whom section ("Interaction
type: conversational"): an ask is brought in conversation, and the
route is decided and read there. The core-task list carries no entry
for making a request; the initiative's Feasibility and usability
section holds "make a request" as a core-task entry in hypothesis, the
product designer role's to settle.

The hypothesis the designer's criteria stand on, matching the
initiative's Feasibility and usability section (designer,
2026-09-04): *make a request* is a core-task entry holding on every
interaction type — an originator states an ask, and it is recorded
and routed — with three options every type offering it must present:
state the ask in the originator's words; see the request's id; see
its route (a discovery conversation, the small-change lane, declined)
and its reason. The conversational door is an assistant interaction
(glossary): the product acts on the stated intent, so the router says
the route before acting and the originator can correct it
(`control-stays-with-the-person`). Like every entry on the list it is
a hypothesis with no observed use; it enters the core-task list
through the corpus's own change, not this feature, and user research
confirms or removes it.

1	---
2	type: artifact-typedef
3	id: feature-typedef
4	defines: feature
5	owner: product-authority
6	status: approved
7	approved: 2026-08-31
8	version: 12
9	created: 2026-08-26
10	updated: 2026-09-04
11	ancestry: [feature]
12	---
13	
14	# Artifact type: feature
15	
16	## Identity and ancestry
17	
18	- **Type:** `feature` — a Gherkin Feature: one capability described
19	  from the user's or agent's point of view, with the scenarios that
20	  state, as requirements, what counts as done for it. A product-level
21	  artifact: it belongs to the [initiative](initiative.md) it is made
22	  from — or, when small, to the [request](request.md) routed to the
23	  small-change lane it is made from — and may hold scenarios owned by
24	  several Bounded Contexts. The scenario is the atom; the feature is
25	  its grouping; the feature repository — the lead shop's directory of
26	  feature artifacts — is the record of what is specified, and a
27	  context's assigned set is the subset of scenarios, across all
28	  features, tagged to it. The instance is a
29	  markdown document with frontmatter whose Scenarios section holds one
30	  fenced Gherkin block — the executable unit the shops receive; the
31	  other sections are the document's, not Gherkin's. Scenarios are
32	  executed by the owning shops; the feature as a document is judged by
33	  the [feature fitness set](../fitness/feature.fitness.md), never
34	  executed there. `ancestry` names no generic root: a feature is
35	  neither a request nor a definition.
36	- **Produced by:** the [PO role](../roles/lead-po.md), as sole author —
37	  the scenarios' steps included; the product designer role contributes
38	  usability and accessibility criteria, the solutions architect role
39	  its non-functional constraints where the decomposition names them.
40	  The owning shops do not co-author: conflicts with behavior already
41	  specified are caught by the repository sweep at assignment, and a
42	  shop's objection travels as a clarify or a returned dispatch after
43	  it receives its scenarios. Checked by the
44	  [PO output check](../processes/po-output-check.md); its scenarios
45	  assigned to Bounded Contexts by the solutions architect role in the
46	  [scenario assignment](../processes/scenario-assignment.md) process.
47	  **Consumed by:** the shops, each receiving the scenarios tagged to it;
48	  the [interaction conformance check](../processes/interaction-conformance-check.md)
49	  for the interaction types named; the changelog rendering the same report proposes, when the
50	  [reconcile-and-close](../processes/reconcile-and-close.md) process
51	  closes the work that delivered its scenarios.
52	
53	## Required frontmatter
54	
55	`type: feature`, `id`, `status`, `version`, `name` (the Feature's
56	name), `initiative` (link to the initiative it is made from; its
57	framing is that document's first section), `owner`, `created`,
58	`updated`; `size` — `standard` | `small`, `standard` when absent.
59	When `size: small`, `request` (link to the request routed to the
60	small-change lane the feature is made from) stands in place of
61	`initiative`, and the framing is that request's section 1 (What is
62	requested): the PO output check's `framing` input names that section
63	for a small feature, and its record step has no initiative to activate.
64	`approved` does not apply: a feature's terminal state is
65	`assigned`. Status values and their writers: `draft` (the PO role);
66	`checked`, `returned`, `pending-definition` (the PO output check's
67	record step, replacing `draft`); a returned or pending feature the PO
68	role resubmits goes back to `draft`; `assigned` (the scenario
69	assignment process's record step, replacing `checked` when every
70	scenario carries its tag); a feature the assignment process returns
71	goes to `returned`.
72	
73	## Required sections
74	
75	1. **Feature** — the Gherkin `Feature:` line with its name, and the
76	   narrative beneath it: who the capability is for, what they can do,
77	   and the outcome it serves, in the framing's words.
78	2. **Contributors** — for every scenario, the owning shop named — the
79	   shop the solutions architect's decomposition places the behavior in
80	   (ownership for assignment, not authorship); where the capability has
81	   an interaction, the product designer role's usability acceptance
82	   criteria and the accessibility criteria; where the decomposition
83	   names them, the solutions architect role's non-functional
84	   constraints, riding as criteria on the scenarios they bound.
85	3. **Interaction types** — always present: the interaction types the
86	   capability must be available on, from the
87	   [core-task list](../experience/core-tasks.md), or "none" with the
88	   reason when the capability has no interaction.
89	4. **Scenarios** — one fenced `gherkin` block, the executable unit:
90	   it opens with the `Feature:` line and narrative of §1 verbatim (§1
91	   is the document's reading of the block's head; the block is the
92	   source, and the repeat is accepted so the document reads without
93	   the block), then an optional `Background:` (its Given steps judged as any
94	   step), then each `Scenario:` carrying the tags `@feature:<id>` (so a
95	   scenario travels alone to a shop and still names its feature —
96	   the reason the Feature line's tag inheritance is not relied on),
97	   `@hash:<sha>` (a hash of the scenario's text), and, once assigned,
98	   `@bounded-context:<name>`; Given/When/Then with one action or event
99	   in the When and an outcome observable in the running system in the
100	   Then; no step names an implementation detail.
101	5. **Edges** — a table of every failure and boundary case the framing
102	   or a contributor's criteria name: case · who named it · the
103	   `Scenario:` name that covers it, or "out of scope" with the reason.
104	
105	## Rules
106	
107	- A scenario's `@bounded-context:` tag is written by the solutions
108	  architect role at assignment, never by the PO role — a writer rule
109	  the assignment process enforces; the check does not judge the tag's
110	  presence, since a re-verified or resubmitted feature may carry it. In
111	  the assignment process, a scenario whose owning context differs from
112	  its Contributors' shop is treated as unowned with that reason, so the
113	  feature returns (`returned`) for the PO role to correct the owning
114	  shop it names.
115	- A changed scenario text is a new scenario with a new `@hash:`.
116	  Whether the hash matches the text is a mechanical check, to be filed
117	  as a lint.
118	- A scenario's conflicts with behavior already specified are caught
119	  by the sweep of the feature repository at assignment, never by
120	  asking the shop during authoring; the shop's voice after dispatch
121	  is the clarify and the return.
122	- A small feature (`size: small`) is made from a request routed to the
123	  small-change lane when the change is best expressed as scenarios;
124	  the lane's definition step may produce one, the PO role its author
125	  as for any feature. It links its `request` in place of an
126	  initiative, is framed by the request's section 1, and is otherwise
127	  a feature: the same sections, scenario and hash rules, check, and
128	  assignment; no bet and no check of record stand between the request
129	  and it.
130	
131	## Commitment (Definition of Done)
132	
133	A feature is done when it has passed the PO output check against its
134	fitness set and the framing, and every scenario carries a
135	`@bounded-context:` tag. **Consequence on failure:** it is returned
136	with the criterion named and no scenario is dispatched.
137	
138	## Sources
139	
140	Gherkin (Feature, narrative, Background, Scenario, tags — the block's
141	form); the
142	experience principles `core-task-parity` and `accessible-by-standard`.
143	
144	## Derived review checklist
145	
146	- Feature line and narrative present, tied to the framing. *(§Required sections 1; fitness 6)*
147	- Each scenario one observable behavior, no how. *(§Required sections 4; fitness 1)*
148	- Every scenario has a named owning shop; designer criteria where there is an interaction; architect constraints where named. *(§Required sections 2; fitness 2)*
149	- `@feature:` and `@hash:` on every scenario. *(§Required sections 4; fitness 3)*
150	- Every listed edge covered or excluded with reason. *(§Required sections 5; fitness 4)*
151	- Interaction types section present, named or "none" with reason. *(§Required sections 3; fitness 5)*
152	- `size` absent or `standard` with `initiative` linked; or `small` with `request` linked in its place, the framing the request's section 1. *(§Required frontmatter; §Rules)*
153

# Artifact type: feature

## Identity and ancestry

- **Type:** `feature` — a Gherkin Feature: one capability described
  from the user's or agent's point of view, with the scenarios that
  state, as requirements, what counts as done for it. A product-level
  artifact: it belongs to the [initiative](initiative.md) it is made
  from — or, when small, to the [request](request.md) routed to the
  small-change lane it is made from — and may hold scenarios owned by
  several Bounded Contexts. The scenario is the atom; the feature is
  its grouping; the feature repository — the lead shop's directory of
  feature artifacts — is the record of what is specified, and a
  context's assigned set is the subset of scenarios, across all
  features, tagged to it. The instance is a
  markdown document with frontmatter whose Scenarios section holds one
  fenced Gherkin block — the executable unit the shops receive; the
  other sections are the document's, not Gherkin's. Scenarios are
  executed by the owning shops; the feature as a document is judged by
  the [feature fitness set](../fitness/feature.fitness.md), never
  executed there. `ancestry` names no generic root: a feature is
  neither a request nor a definition.
- **Produced by:** the [PO role](../roles/lead-po.md), as sole author —
  the scenarios' steps included; the product designer role contributes
  usability and accessibility criteria, the solutions architect role
  its non-functional constraints where the decomposition names them.
  The owning shops do not co-author: conflicts with behavior already
  specified are caught by the repository sweep at assignment, and a
  shop's objection travels as a clarify or a returned dispatch after
  it receives its scenarios. Checked by the
  [PO output check](../processes/po-output-check.md); its scenarios
  assigned to Bounded Contexts by the solutions architect role in the
  [scenario assignment](../processes/scenario-assignment.md) process.
  **Consumed by:** the shops, each receiving the scenarios tagged to it;
  the [interaction conformance check](../processes/interaction-conformance-check.md)
  for the interaction types named; the changelog rendering the same report proposes, when the
  [reconcile-and-close](../processes/reconcile-and-close.md) process
  closes the work that delivered its scenarios.

## Required frontmatter

`type: feature`, `id`, `status`, `version`, `name` (the Feature's
name), `initiative` (link to the initiative it is made from; its
framing is that document's first section), `owner`, `created`,
`updated`; `size` — `standard` | `small`, `standard` when absent.
When `size: small`, `request` (link to the request routed to the
small-change lane the feature is made from) stands in place of
`initiative`, and the framing is that request's section 1 (What is
requested): the PO output check's `framing` input names that section
for a small feature, and its record step has no initiative to activate.
`approved` does not apply: a feature's terminal state is
`assigned`. Status values and their writers: `draft` (the PO role);
`checked`, `returned`, `pending-definition` (the PO output check's
record step, replacing `draft`); a returned or pending feature the PO
role resubmits goes back to `draft`; `assigned` (the scenario
assignment process's record step, replacing `checked` when every
scenario carries its tag); a feature the assignment process returns
goes to `returned`.

## Required sections

1. **Feature** — the Gherkin `Feature:` line with its name, and the
   narrative beneath it: who the capability is for, what they can do,
   and the outcome it serves, in the framing's words.
2. **Contributors** — for every scenario, the owning shop named — the
   shop the solutions architect's decomposition places the behavior in
   (ownership for assignment, not authorship); where the capability has
   an interaction, the product designer role's usability acceptance
   criteria and the accessibility criteria; where the decomposition
   names them, the solutions architect role's non-functional
   constraints, riding as criteria on the scenarios they bound.
3. **Interaction types** — always present: the interaction types the
   capability must be available on, from the
   [core-task list](../experience/core-tasks.md), or "none" with the
   reason when the capability has no interaction.
4. **Scenarios** — one fenced `gherkin` block, the executable unit:
   it opens with the `Feature:` line and narrative of §1 verbatim (§1
   is the document's reading of the block's head; the block is the
   source, and the repeat is accepted so the document reads without
   the block), then an optional `Background:` (its Given steps judged as any
   step), then each `Scenario:` carrying the tags `@feature:<id>` (so a
   scenario travels alone to a shop and still names its feature —
   the reason the Feature line's tag inheritance is not relied on),
   `@hash:<sha>` (a hash of the scenario's text), and, once assigned,
   `@bounded-context:<name>`; Given/When/Then with one action or event
   in the When and an outcome observable in the running system in the
   Then; no step names an implementation detail.
5. **Edges** — a table of every failure and boundary case the framing
   or a contributor's criteria name: case · who named it · the
   `Scenario:` name that covers it, or "out of scope" with the reason.

## Rules

- A scenario's `@bounded-context:` tag is written by the solutions
  architect role at assignment, never by the PO role — a writer rule
  the assignment process enforces; the check does not judge the tag's
  presence, since a re-verified or resubmitted feature may carry it. In
  the assignment process, a scenario whose owning context differs from
  its Contributors' shop is treated as unowned with that reason, so the
  feature returns (`returned`) for the PO role to correct the owning
  shop it names.
- A changed scenario text is a new scenario with a new `@hash:`.
  Whether the hash matches the text is a mechanical check, to be filed
  as a lint.
- A scenario's conflicts with behavior already specified are caught
  by the sweep of the feature repository at assignment, never by
  asking the shop during authoring; the shop's voice after dispatch
  is the clarify and the return.
- A small feature (`size: small`) is made from a request routed to the
  small-change lane when the change is best expressed as scenarios;
  the lane's definition step may produce one, the PO role its author
  as for any feature. It links its `request` in place of an
  initiative, is framed by the request's section 1, and is otherwise
  a feature: the same sections, scenario and hash rules, check, and
  assignment; no bet and no check of record stand between the request
  and it.

## Commitment (Definition of Done)

A feature is done when it has passed the PO output check against its
fitness set and the framing, and every scenario carries a
`@bounded-context:` tag. **Consequence on failure:** it is returned
with the criterion named and no scenario is dispatched.

## Sources

Gherkin (Feature, narrative, Background, Scenario, tags — the block's
form); the
experience principles `core-task-parity` and `accessible-by-standard`.

## Derived review checklist

- Feature line and narrative present, tied to the framing. *(§Required sections 1; fitness 6)*
- Each scenario one observable behavior, no how. *(§Required sections 4; fitness 1)*
- Every scenario has a named owning shop; designer criteria where there is an interaction; architect constraints where named. *(§Required sections 2; fitness 2)*
- `@feature:` and `@hash:` on every scenario. *(§Required sections 4; fitness 3)*
- Every listed edge covered or excluded with reason. *(§Required sections 5; fitness 4)*
- Interaction types section present, named or "none" with reason. *(§Required sections 3; fitness 5)*
- `size` absent or `standard` with `initiative` linked; or `small` with `request` linked in its place, the framing the request's section 1. *(§Required frontmatter; §Rules)*

# Feature: Roles availability

## Feature

Feature: Roles availability
  An agent of the lead shop filling a named role in a process step
  can load the approved definition of that role at its point of work,
  from an approved source that is itself maintained by a defined
  process with its own check,
  so that no role the agent runtime instantiates comes from an
  unapproved source: the agent operates from the approved definition
  of its role.

## Contributors

Owning shop, per scenario — from the initiative's Decomposition
section, which names no Bounded Context: the source definitions, the
render, and the load point all sit in the lead shop's own tree.

- *an approved role definition is available at the point of work* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *an agent fills a role from the approved source at the point of work* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *a role definition that does not stand approved yields no available role* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *a role in the approved source not current with its approved definition is detected* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *an approved role definition with no available role is reported* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)

1	---
2	type: adr
3	id: adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering
4	title: An artifact type's typedef is its one hand-edited standard; its guideline and fitness set are renderings of it
5	status: checked
6	version: 4
7	date: 2026-09-05
8	decided-by: product-authority
9	right: escalation
10	owner: lead-solutions-architect
11	created: 2026-09-05
12	updated: 2026-09-05
13	---
14	
15	# ADR: An artifact type's typedef is its one hand-edited standard; its guideline and fitness set are renderings of it
16	
17	## 1. Context
18	
19	This repository is the lead shop: the coordinating shop of the product,
20	owning the product-level definitions under `basis/` (the definition
21	corpus) and no Bounded Context — a region of the product with its own
22	model, built by a shop of its own, a BC shop. An artifact type is a kind
23	of document the shop produces. Three definitions carry a type's standard
24	of good. The *typedef* (type key `artifact-typedef`) defines the type:
25	identity, required frontmatter, required sections, commitment, sources,
26	a derived review checklist. The *guideline* (type key
27	`quality-guideline`) holds the writing rules as prose, each with a test,
28	a criterion, a yes/no decision, and the fitness scenario it feeds; its
29	Highlights block is the layer loaded into an author's context. The
30	*fitness set* (type key `fitness-set`) holds Given/When/Then scenarios a
31	judge — the cold-reviewer role — scores an instance against, with a
32	Compile mapping table taking each scenario into one judge assertion;
33	judged, never run by a test runner.
34	
35	Pre-state, 2026-09-05, as the request — the record of an ask on arrival
36	— states it
37	([req-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering](../requests/req-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering.md)):
38	22 typedefs, 17 guidelines, 11 fitness sets, all hand-written, none
39	generated, no compiler. Of those, 10 guidelines and 10 fitness sets have
40	an artifact type with a typedef behind them, and they belong to the same
41	ten types, so 12 of the 22 typedefs have neither; the other 7 guidelines
42	(the base writing style and the six experience guidelines) and 1
43	fitness set (interaction) have no artifact type behind them. The proof
44	slice — the first feature, one type converted and used by a whole
45	process run — is the product decision record, written by the PO role,
46	the lead shop's product owner ("Okay, use the pdr"). Its typedef (v6),
47	[guideline](../basis/guidelines/product-decision-record.md) (v2), and
48	[fitness set](../basis/fitness/product-decision-record.fitness.md) (v3)
49	carry the same five rules, each with its own history. The
50	[artifact-typedef typedef](../basis/artifacts/artifact-typedef.md) (v2)
51	already rules: "Templates, schema fragments, and validators are its
52	renderings; the typedef is the only hand-edited form." The rule says one
53	hand-edited form; the practice keeps three.
54	
55	Forces. The authority, in the request and in the discovery conversation
56	that framed the initiative
57	([sess-2026-09-05-a](../sessions/sess-2026-09-05-a.md)): "the typdef
58	[sic] included everything including guidelines and fitness checks and those
59	were just renderings"; "The tests should stay as is, executable by the
60	author and a check if necessary … rendered out to whatever format works
61	well for inclusion in prompts" — "executable" meaning applied by a
62	reader, the scenarios staying judged. `single-source-of-truth`, from the
63	[working principle set](../basis/principles.md): one home per fact,
64	every other appearance a reference or a generated rendering; today the
65	standard has three homes.
66	
67	Evidence that the checks read by path: the PO output check — run by the
68	lead-pm role, the lead shop's product manager — takes `criteria_path`,
69	"the approved fitness set or guideline for the artifact's type"
70	([po-output-check](../basis/processes/po-output-check.md), Data).
71	Evidence for the pattern:
72	[`compile_process.py`](../basis/tools/compile_process.py) renders a
73	process definition into its skill (the file an agent loads to run it)
74	stamped `source-digest: sha256:` plus twelve hex digits of the source
75	text's hash — the stamp tying a rendering to its exact source — and
76	`compile_role.py` adds `--check`, a fresh render compared with the
77	committed file, a difference being drift. Each compiler runs under a
78	rendering process: skill-rendering runs compile_process.py,
79	role-rendering runs compile_role.py, and this decision adds a third
80	process for its compiler. The lead shop's compilers are interim
81	tooling, kept only while the shop renders its own definitions.
82	
83	**The escalation that settled it.** The decision is the authority's,
84	so it records under `right: escalation`: none of the five rights the
85	solutions architect role holds — stack, guardrail (a bound on BC
86	shops), decomposition, contract between Bounded Contexts,
87	non-functional requirement — covers which document of the shop's own
88	corpus is hand-edited and which are produced from it. The
89	authority ruled on 2026-09-05 — "The typedef rendering should go
90	first. It should be made into a request and follow that process" —
91	and in the discovery conversation on that request said "Converged".
92	The initiative
93	[init-typedef-rendering](../initiatives/init-typedef-rendering.md)
94	carries the framing; its feasibility attachment, the architect's,
95	named this decision as the one the bet — the authority's go or no-go
96	on it — rests on.
97	
98	Options that were real:
99	
100	- **Keep three hand-written documents; add a consistency check.**
101	  Declined: three homes remain, and drift is found after the fact.
102	- **Point the checks at the typedef; retire the two documents.**
103	  Declined: the judge reads the criteria set and nothing else, and the
104	  typedef carries identity, sources, and history it does not need
105	  (`least-context`, the working principle of loading the minimum); and
106	  every check's parameter changes — the initiative's first no-go
107	  condition, what it will not do: "any change to the checking
108	  processes themselves".
109	- **Make the fitness set the source.** Declined: scenarios do not yield
110	  identity, sections, commitment, or sources, and the artifact-typedef
111	  typedef already names the typedef the only hand-edited form.
112	- **Render at check time, commit nothing.** Declined: text made inside a
113	  step is context from a source the process does not name
114	  (`least-context`); the linter — `basis/tools/lint_basis.py`, the
115	  check the tree runs on every definition — reads files on disk; the
116	  first no-go condition again.
117	
118	Not decided here: four follow-on questions are listed in this record's
119	Document History (v4).
120	
121	## 2. Decision
122	
123	An artifact type's typedef is the one hand-edited document of that
124	type's standard: it carries the type's writing rules and its fitness
125	scenarios as sections, and the type's guideline and fitness set are
126	produced from it by a compiler on the compile_process.py pattern,
127	written at the paths the checks already read, each stamped with the
128	source-digest of the typedef it was produced from.
129	
130	## Principles screen
131	
132	Screened against the
133	[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
134	conforms on five; `intent-provenance` rests on the exception
135	[adr-2026-09-04-request-front-end](adr-2026-09-04-request-front-end.md)
136	carries, escalated to the authority (work item lead-4kymc).
137	`knowable-shape` — which document is authored and which produced is
138	readable from the typedefs and the renderings' frontmatter.
139	`contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context is touched.
140	`actor-neutral-discipline` — the compiler yields the same text whoever
141	runs it; a hand edit of a rendering is drift whoever made it.
142	`local-comprehension` — maker and judge read the rendering for their
143	step, the definition author the typedef. `bidirectional-conformance` —
144	this record precedes the compiler; forward, the initiative's measure
145	(1 of 22, then 22 of 22); reverse, a rendering whose digest does not
146	match its source is regenerated or removed. `intent-provenance` — the
147	request, its route, the initiative, and this record are each recorded;
148	the entry contract the request names has no artifact yet — the cited
149	exception.
150	
151	## 3. Consequences
152	
153	- The typedef is the only document a definition author edits. What
154	  changes: each typedef gains two sections, the writing rules and the
155	  fitness scenarios, and the artifact-typedef typedef amends to require
156	  them. For whom: the product authority, who owns and approves every
157	  typedef; definition authors. Cost: the amendment; one typedef
158	  converted for the proof, then twenty-one as one batch; a longer
159	  typedef to read. Forecloses: a hand edit of a guideline or a fitness
160	  set — it is drift, and the next render overwrites it.
161	- The guideline and the fitness set become renderings. What changes:
162	  each carries `generated: true`, `generated-by`, `derived-from`,
163	  `source`, and `source-digest`, and no version or Document History of
164	  its own; the quality-guideline and fitness-set typedefs amend to name
165	  the compiler as producer while keeping the shape the checks read —
166	  a rendering is still a `quality-guideline` or a `fitness-set` with
167	  its `target-type`, its Highlights, its Scenarios and Compile
168	  mapping. For whom: the cold-reviewer role, which reads the fitness
169	  set at `criteria_path`; makers, who read the guideline's Highlights;
170	  the linter, which derives the chain from the frontmatter. Cost: two
171	  typedef amendments; the past history of the 10 guidelines and 10
172	  fitness sets converted stops at the conversion and stays readable only in
173	  source control, the typedef's Document History carrying the
174	  standard's changes from then on. Forecloses: a guideline or fitness
175	  set that says something its typedef does not.
176	- A compiler joins the lead shop's tools. What changes: a script on
177	  the compile_process.py pattern parses a typedef, writes the two
178	  texts, stamps each with the source-digest, and offers a check that
179	  compares the committed renderings with a fresh render. For whom:
180	  whoever runs the rendering process; the architect role, which
181	  maintains the shop's tools. Cost: one script; one rendering process
182	  definition with its check step and its own skill; a render after
183	  every typedef change. Forecloses: nothing — the script is interim
184	  tooling, retired when the shop stops rendering its own definitions.
185	- The checks stay as they are. What changes: nothing in the PO output
186	  check, adr-authoring, feature-authoring, or the linter — each reads
187	  the path it reads today and finds a rendering there. For whom: the
188	  cold-reviewer role; the lead-pm role, which decides from the review.
189	  Cost: the rendering must keep the type keys and headings the checks
190	  and the linter require; a renderer that drops one breaks a check
191	  without changing it.
192	- A change to a standard is one edit and one render. What changes: the
193	  authority or a definition author changes the typedef, the render
194	  runs, and maker and judge read the same words. For whom: the
195	  authority, evaluating a type's standard in one place; every maker
196	  and checker of the type. Cost: a rendering behind its source is
197	  drift until the next render, and the check step is what finds it.
198	
199	Bound on Bounded Context shops: none — the definition corpus is the
200	lead shop's; a BC shop's own definitions stand under its own
201	operational contract. Extending this rule to BC shops would be a
202	guardrail decision, the architect role's.
203	
204	## 4. Reversibility
205	
206	Reversible at low cost while one type is converted: the two renderings
207	are still documents of their types, so reverting is removing the two
208	sections from the typedef, restoring the guideline's and fitness set's
209	frontmatter and history from source control, and deleting the
210	compiler. Hard after the batch: twenty-two typedefs carry the rules
211	and scenarios, the renderings — two per converted type — carry no
212	history of their own, and each reversal is a per-document
213	reconstruction from source control, and any process or role that has
214	come to cite a typedef's rules section by number must re-point. Review triggers: the shop stops rendering
215	its own definitions, so the compiler has no source to read; a check needs a criteria set the typedef cannot carry as
216	a section; the three rendering processes' shared shape makes a
217	generalization cheaper than a third sibling (lead-sx9xj); the base
218	writing style or the experience guidelines need a source of their own;
219	a converted typedef grows past what its author reads in one sitting —
220	under `local-comprehension`, a design defect to repair, not a reader's

---
type: adr
id: adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering
title: An artifact type's typedef is its one hand-edited standard; its guideline and fitness set are renderings of it
status: checked
version: 4
date: 2026-09-05
decided-by: product-authority
right: escalation
owner: lead-solutions-architect
created: 2026-09-05
updated: 2026-09-05
---

# ADR: An artifact type's typedef is its one hand-edited standard; its guideline and fitness set are renderings of it

## 1. Context

This repository is the lead shop: the coordinating shop of the product,
owning the product-level definitions under `basis/` (the definition
corpus) and no Bounded Context — a region of the product with its own
model, built by a shop of its own, a BC shop. An artifact type is a kind
of document the shop produces. Three definitions carry a type's standard
of good. The *typedef* (type key `artifact-typedef`) defines the type:
identity, required frontmatter, required sections, commitment, sources,
a derived review checklist. The *guideline* (type key
`quality-guideline`) holds the writing rules as prose, each with a test,
a criterion, a yes/no decision, and the fitness scenario it feeds; its
Highlights block is the layer loaded into an author's context. The
*fitness set* (type key `fitness-set`) holds Given/When/Then scenarios a
judge — the cold-reviewer role — scores an instance against, with a
Compile mapping table taking each scenario into one judge assertion;
judged, never run by a test runner.

Pre-state, 2026-09-05, as the request — the record of an ask on arrival
— states it
([req-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering](../requests/req-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering.md)):
22 typedefs, 17 guidelines, 11 fitness sets, all hand-written, none
generated, no compiler. Of those, 10 guidelines and 10 fitness sets have
an artifact type with a typedef behind them, and they belong to the same
ten types, so 12 of the 22 typedefs have neither; the other 7 guidelines
(the base writing style and the six experience guidelines) and 1
fitness set (interaction) have no artifact type behind them. The proof
slice — the first feature, one type converted and used by a whole
process run — is the product decision record, written by the PO role,
the lead shop's product owner ("Okay, use the pdr"). Its typedef (v6),
[guideline](../basis/guidelines/product-decision-record.md) (v2), and
[fitness set](../basis/fitness/product-decision-record.fitness.md) (v3)
carry the same five rules, each with its own history. The
[artifact-typedef typedef](../basis/artifacts/artifact-typedef.md) (v2)
already rules: "Templates, schema fragments, and validators are its
renderings; the typedef is the only hand-edited form." The rule says one
hand-edited form; the practice keeps three.

Forces. The authority, in the request and in the discovery conversation
that framed the initiative
([sess-2026-09-05-a](../sessions/sess-2026-09-05-a.md)): "the typdef
[sic] included everything including guidelines and fitness checks and those
were just renderings"; "The tests should stay as is, executable by the
author and a check if necessary … rendered out to whatever format works
well for inclusion in prompts" — "executable" meaning applied by a
reader, the scenarios staying judged. `single-source-of-truth`, from the
[working principle set](../basis/principles.md): one home per fact,
every other appearance a reference or a generated rendering; today the
standard has three homes.

Evidence that the checks read by path: the PO output check — run by the
lead-pm role, the lead shop's product manager — takes `criteria_path`,
"the approved fitness set or guideline for the artifact's type"
([po-output-check](../basis/processes/po-output-check.md), Data).
Evidence for the pattern:
[`compile_process.py`](../basis/tools/compile_process.py) renders a
process definition into its skill (the file an agent loads to run it)
stamped `source-digest: sha256:` plus twelve hex digits of the source
text's hash — the stamp tying a rendering to its exact source — and
`compile_role.py` adds `--check`, a fresh render compared with the
committed file, a difference being drift. Each compiler runs under a
rendering process: skill-rendering runs compile_process.py,
role-rendering runs compile_role.py, and this decision adds a third
process for its compiler. The lead shop's compilers are interim
tooling, kept only while the shop renders its own definitions.

**The escalation that settled it.** The decision is the authority's,
so it records under `right: escalation`: none of the five rights the
solutions architect role holds — stack, guardrail (a bound on BC
shops), decomposition, contract between Bounded Contexts,
non-functional requirement — covers which document of the shop's own
corpus is hand-edited and which are produced from it. The
authority ruled on 2026-09-05 — "The typedef rendering should go
first. It should be made into a request and follow that process" —
and in the discovery conversation on that request said "Converged".
The initiative
[init-typedef-rendering](../initiatives/init-typedef-rendering.md)
carries the framing; its feasibility attachment, the architect's,
named this decision as the one the bet — the authority's go or no-go
on it — rests on.

Options that were real:

- **Keep three hand-written documents; add a consistency check.**
  Declined: three homes remain, and drift is found after the fact.
- **Point the checks at the typedef; retire the two documents.**
  Declined: the judge reads the criteria set and nothing else, and the
  typedef carries identity, sources, and history it does not need
  (`least-context`, the working principle of loading the minimum); and
  every check's parameter changes — the initiative's first no-go
  condition, what it will not do: "any change to the checking
  processes themselves".
- **Make the fitness set the source.** Declined: scenarios do not yield
  identity, sections, commitment, or sources, and the artifact-typedef
  typedef already names the typedef the only hand-edited form.
- **Render at check time, commit nothing.** Declined: text made inside a
  step is context from a source the process does not name
  (`least-context`); the linter — `basis/tools/lint_basis.py`, the
  check the tree runs on every definition — reads files on disk; the
  first no-go condition again.

Not decided here: four follow-on questions are listed in this record's
Document History (v4).

## 2. Decision

An artifact type's typedef is the one hand-edited document of that
type's standard: it carries the type's writing rules and its fitness
scenarios as sections, and the type's guideline and fitness set are
produced from it by a compiler on the compile_process.py pattern,
written at the paths the checks already read, each stamped with the
source-digest of the typedef it was produced from.

## Principles screen

Screened against the
[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
conforms on five; `intent-provenance` rests on the exception
[adr-2026-09-04-request-front-end](adr-2026-09-04-request-front-end.md)
carries, escalated to the authority (work item lead-4kymc).
`knowable-shape` — which document is authored and which produced is
readable from the typedefs and the renderings' frontmatter.
`contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context is touched.
`actor-neutral-discipline` — the compiler yields the same text whoever
runs it; a hand edit of a rendering is drift whoever made it.
`local-comprehension` — maker and judge read the rendering for their
step, the definition author the typedef. `bidirectional-conformance` —
this record precedes the compiler; forward, the initiative's measure
(1 of 22, then 22 of 22); reverse, a rendering whose digest does not
match its source is regenerated or removed. `intent-provenance` — the
request, its route, the initiative, and this record are each recorded;
the entry contract the request names has no artifact yet — the cited
exception.

## 3. Consequences

- The typedef is the only document a definition author edits. What
  changes: each typedef gains two sections, the writing rules and the
  fitness scenarios, and the artifact-typedef typedef amends to require
  them. For whom: the product authority, who owns and approves every
  typedef; definition authors. Cost: the amendment; one typedef
  converted for the proof, then twenty-one as one batch; a longer
  typedef to read. Forecloses: a hand edit of a guideline or a fitness
  set — it is drift, and the next render overwrites it.
- The guideline and the fitness set become renderings. What changes:
  each carries `generated: true`, `generated-by`, `derived-from`,
  `source`, and `source-digest`, and no version or Document History of
  its own; the quality-guideline and fitness-set typedefs amend to name
  the compiler as producer while keeping the shape the checks read —
  a rendering is still a `quality-guideline` or a `fitness-set` with
  its `target-type`, its Highlights, its Scenarios and Compile
  mapping. For whom: the cold-reviewer role, which reads the fitness
  set at `criteria_path`; makers, who read the guideline's Highlights;
  the linter, which derives the chain from the frontmatter. Cost: two
  typedef amendments; the past history of the 10 guidelines and 10
  fitness sets converted stops at the conversion and stays readable only in
  source control, the typedef's Document History carrying the
  standard's changes from then on. Forecloses: a guideline or fitness
  set that says something its typedef does not.
- A compiler joins the lead shop's tools. What changes: a script on
  the compile_process.py pattern parses a typedef, writes the two
  texts, stamps each with the source-digest, and offers a check that
  compares the committed renderings with a fresh render. For whom:
  whoever runs the rendering process; the architect role, which
  maintains the shop's tools. Cost: one script; one rendering process
  definition with its check step and its own skill; a render after
  every typedef change. Forecloses: nothing — the script is interim
  tooling, retired when the shop stops rendering its own definitions.
- The checks stay as they are. What changes: nothing in the PO output
  check, adr-authoring, feature-authoring, or the linter — each reads
  the path it reads today and finds a rendering there. For whom: the
  cold-reviewer role; the lead-pm role, which decides from the review.
  Cost: the rendering must keep the type keys and headings the checks
  and the linter require; a renderer that drops one breaks a check
  without changing it.
- A change to a standard is one edit and one render. What changes: the
  authority or a definition author changes the typedef, the render
  runs, and maker and judge read the same words. For whom: the
  authority, evaluating a type's standard in one place; every maker
  and checker of the type. Cost: a rendering behind its source is
  drift until the next render, and the check step is what finds it.

Bound on Bounded Context shops: none — the definition corpus is the
lead shop's; a BC shop's own definitions stand under its own
operational contract. Extending this rule to BC shops would be a
guardrail decision, the architect role's.

## 4. Reversibility

Reversible at low cost while one type is converted: the two renderings
are still documents of their types, so reverting is removing the two
sections from the typedef, restoring the guideline's and fitness set's
frontmatter and history from source control, and deleting the
compiler. Hard after the batch: twenty-two typedefs carry the rules
and scenarios, the renderings — two per converted type — carry no
history of their own, and each reversal is a per-document
reconstruction from source control, and any process or role that has
come to cite a typedef's rules section by number must re-point. Review triggers: the shop stops rendering
its own definitions, so the compiler has no source to read; a check needs a criteria set the typedef cannot carry as
a section; the three rendering processes' shared shape makes a
generalization cheaper than a third sibling (lead-sx9xj); the base
writing style or the experience guidelines need a source of their own;
a converted typedef grows past what its author reads in one sitting —
under `local-comprehension`, a design defect to repair, not a reader's
burden.

   with the reason it was not.

  home with the adr type, the filename prefix and the frontmatter
  `type` discriminating; which type records a decision is decided by
  the right exercised, per the rule the

  ruling at the check, not the record's claim; a record whose decider
  is the authority is checked for form only.

A record is done when it has passed the PO output check against its
fitness set and the framing. **Consequence on failure:** it is returned with the
criterion named and binds nothing.

Nygard's architecture decision record (decision, consequences); MADR
(considered alternatives); decider and reversibility as the shop's own
additions, from the roles' decision rights; the
[product-decision-record fitness set](../fitness/product-decision-record.fitness.md).

- One decision, actionable. *(§Required sections 1; fitness 1)*
- A real alternative with its reason. *(§Required sections 2; fitness 2)*
- Decider and right, or the escalation, named. *(§Required frontmatter; fitness 3)*
- Each consequence names what changes, for whom, at what cost. *(§Required sections 3; fitness 4)*

# Feature: Typedef rendering

## Feature

Feature: Typedef rendering
  The makers and checkers of every artifact type, and the authority
  when the standard changes,
  can work from one standard for an artifact type — the maker's text
  and the checker's text both from it, a change to the standard
  reaching both, and the checker's tests runnable by the author
  first —
  so that whoever makes an artifact and whoever checks it work from
  the same standard, and when the standard changes it reaches both.

## Contributors

Owning shop, per scenario — from the initiative's Decomposition
section, which names no Bounded Context: the standard, the two texts,
and the checks that read them sit in the lead shop's tree, and no
contract exists on this branch to rely on.

- *the maker's text and the checker's text for a type come from its one standard* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *an author runs the checker's tests on their own draft before the check* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *a change to the standard reaches the maker's text and the checker's text* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *a text not current with its standard is reported* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *a type with no maker's text or no checker's text has both once its standard states them* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *a type whose standard states that no text is due has none and is not reported* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *a check screens against the produced text as it did before* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
- *the product decision record of this initiative's bet is made and checked from one standard* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)

Vocabulary: *standard* is the framing's word for what the maker and
the checker of an artifact of a type work from — the type's writing
rules and the tests an instance is checked against; which document of
the lead shop's tree is that standard is the design decision the
initiative rests on
([adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering](../decisions/adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering.md)),
not this feature's to say. The *maker's text* is what a maker of an
artifact of the type reads for its writing rules — the glossary's
`guideline`. The *checker's text* is what a check of an artifact of
the type screens it against — the glossary's `fitness set`: judged
Given/When/Then scenarios, the *checker's tests*. A text is *produced
from* a standard when it is, in the glossary's term, a rendering of
it — never edited by hand, never the source — and *current with* the
standard when the standard has not changed since the text was
produced from it; a text names the standard it is produced from, so a
reader can tell both from the text. *The check over the texts* is the
check that reads each text against its standard and reports one that
is not current, distinct from the checks that screen an artifact
against the checker's text (the PO output check among them); it
belongs to the process that keeps the texts current. *The proof* is
the initiative's Appetite: the product decision record of this
initiative's bet, made by the PO role from the maker's text and
screened by its check against the checker's text, the check's use
counting whether or not it screens for form only.

## Interaction types

None — the standard is read inside process steps; no core task
carries it (the initiative's For whom section).

Originator (product authority, 2026-09-05, through the lead shop's
operational contract, which has no artifact yet (lead-4kymc); the
request req-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering; the authority's accepted
restatement of its section 1, on the framer's-wording ruling): "Whoever makes an artifact

Problem: whoever makes an artifact and whoever checks it work from
different words, because the standard for an artifact type is written
in several places by hand, and a change to it does not reliably reach
both. Outcome: the
maker and the checker of an artifact work from the same standard, a
change to the standard reaches both, and the checker's tests, the fitness
set's scenarios, can be run by the author first.

## For whom

The makers and checkers of every artifact type, and the authority when
the standard changes. Measure: artifact types whose maker and checker
work from one standard and have each used it once — the maker to make
an artifact of that type, the check to screen it. Now: 0 of 22.
Target: 1, the product decision record. Interaction types: none — the standard is
read inside process steps; no core task carries it.

## Appetite

One working session of the lead shop for the proof on the product
decision record: the PO role makes this initiative's own bet record
— the product decision record its bet requires — from the same
standard, and the check that screens that record screens it from the
same standard; a form-only screen counts as the check's use.
The other 21 types follow as one batch, a second bet sized after the
proof. No-gos, each with its reason:

- Any change to the checking processes themselves — a later request;
  the checks are not what this bet changes.
- Checking that the standards of different types agree with each
  other — struck by the authority as not needed here.

## Feasibility and usability

Feasible in one session. The three documents — the guideline, the
fitness set, and the typedef's checklist — already match rule for
rule (guideline rule N, fitness scenario N, checklist item N), so
folding them into the typedef is mechanical. The compiler follows
`basis/tools/compile_process.py`: parse the typedef, write two texts,
stamp a `source-digest`. The artifact-typedef typedef already names
such texts renderings. Rendered at the paths the checks read, the
checks stay unchanged. Risk: the bet's record is checked for form
only, a light first run for the checker's text. No contract exists;
no feature touches typedefs. (architect, 2026-09-05)

No usability attachment is due: the For whom section names no
interaction type — the renderings are read inside process steps, and
no core task carries them. (designer, 2026-09-05)

## Decomposition

None: no Bounded Context is touched. The typedef, the compiler, and
the renderings sit in the lead shop's tree; no contract exists on this
branch to rely on. Cross-context flow: none.

None yet.
